youtube_title: Portage, Indiana: the gravestones a 1962 gas station dig turned up (Portage request)
youtube:
You asked for Portage! In July 1962, workmen digging for a new gas station at the corner of US 20 and Crisman Road in Portage turned up three marble stones: a family monument and two headstones for two children of pioneers Isaac and Jane Crisman. Scarlet fever took both children, Wilbur and his sister, in 1876. A Crisman granddaughter said the family cemetery was never at that corner, and she was shown the old township cemetery north of the highway, on a bank overgrown with trees, with no stones showing. How the stones came to be buried at the corner was still unsolved, she told the Vidette-Messenger. Does your family know the rest of the story? Old cemeteries are often on private land: please don't trespass. Comment your town, and it could be next! #Portage #PorterCounty #Indiana #History #LaPorteAfterDark #Shorts

All pictures are drawn. Narration is a computer voice. Sources: Vidette-Messenger (July 11 and July 19, 1962); Porter County Vidette (Dec. 7, 1876); Northwest Indiana Genealogical Society, Portage Township cemetery index (1995); Counties of Porter and Lake (1882); all transcribed at inportercounty.org.
